clue.text: Such craft will work

parts.note: will and shall both mark the future tense
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A promise that boats of this kind will do the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A light open boat once used in shallow waters is one such craft.

clue.text: Security of rank, in eluding lieutenant

indicators.note: including means the word for rank holds the next piece within it

parts.note: rank as in rank folly means sheer, utter

explanation.surface: An officer's job security depends on his rank, and a lieutenant is part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The page as scanned reads 'in eluding', a misreading of 'including', which is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Protection from harm or danger is security in the sense of a safe refuge.

clue.text: The person who thinks he's put on

definitions.text: The person who thinks he's put on

parts.words: The person who thinks he's put on
parts.note: to assume is both to suppose something and to put on clothes or airs, so the one doing it suits both readings

explanation.surface: Someone convinced they are being made fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: One who supposes, or one who takes on a manner, is named after the verb that covers both.

clue.text: Contract for renting house puts student at ease

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate
at ease gives the word ease as written, the relaxed state

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement that relaxes the young tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal agreement letting a property for a period is the tenancy contract.

clue.text: May be portrayed as rapacious

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters of the next word could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone who could be depicted as greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping and preying on others, as a hunting animal does, describes rapacity.

clue.text: Fish assimilating dope go all limp

indicators.note: assimilating means the fish takes the next piece into itself

parts.note: a pout is a kind of fish
a dope, a fool, is an ass

explanation.surface: A fish that has taken in drugs flops over.
explanation.definitionFit: To faint is to lose consciousness and slump limply.

clue.text: Spread over a quarter

parts.note: over as in the summer is over means past
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Something spread across a quarter of the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mixture smeared on bread is a spread such as fish or meat paste.

clue.text: A plant to cover ground quickly to good effect

parts.note: to cover ground quickly is to go at speed, to speed
done to good effect means done well

explanation.surface: A creeping plant that spreads fast and successfully across a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, with small blue flowers, is a common garden plant.

clue.text: Letters dispatched in settlement

parts.note: letters dispatched are sent out
letters collectively are the post, the mail

explanation.surface: Mail sent off to a remote colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A small remote colony or garrison far from the centre is a frontier settlement.

clue.text: Girl with the odd ears

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: odd says the letters of the next word are in a strange order

explanation.surface: A young woman with peculiar ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as a crossword girl, is any woman's given name.

clue.text: French in gin-trap

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: A gin-trap described in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin-trap reads as one device, but gin is the definition: as a verb, to gin is to catch in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: To gin in old usage is to catch an animal in a snare, a synonym for catching.

clue.text: The royal staff demands respect

indicators.note: demands taken as calls for something to be redone, so the letters of the next word are reworked

explanation.surface: The monarch's rod of office commands deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like the royal household's employees, but it is the rod a monarch holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental rod carried by a monarch is the royal staff of office.

clue.text: Clement, evincing some irascibility, took the fare

parts.note: a temper is a fit of irascibility
to take the fare, food, is to eat, so past tense ate

explanation.surface: Clement, showing a little bad temper, ate the meal anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning mild.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild weather is clement and also moderate, as in a mild climate.

clue.text: Livestock went by road transport

definitions.meaning: a herd of cattle being driven
the past tense of driving a car or vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A herd moved in a body is a drove, and the past of driving a vehicle is the same word.

clue.text: The Right are right-that's not so common!

parts.note: R is short for right, the political right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that right-wingers being right is a rare event.
explanation.definitionFit: Less common means less frequent, the comparative of scarce.

clue.text: Forward, but get into line following study

indicators.note: following means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
soldiers dress ranks, getting into line

explanation.surface: An instruction to advance, but only after study and lining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' looks like a military order, but it is the verb for sending mail on to a new address.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on with a new address.

clue.text: Band of gold put on box by a painter

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a chest is a box
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A gold ring put on a box by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band of gold' suggests a ring, but the definition is just 'Band', a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A large group of musicians playing together is a band.

clue.text: Operated turn and turn about in any bottle-neck

definitions.text: Operated turn and turn about in any bottle-neck

parts.words: Operated turn and turn about in any bottle-neck
parts.note: a tool worked by twisting again and again into the neck of a wine bottle, read as a traffic jam

explanation.surface: Drivers taking turns at a traffic bottleneck.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiral tool twisted into a cork in a bottle's neck is described by its action.

clue.text: Most weary after correcting a mischievous boy

indicators.note: correcting suggests the letters of the words before are put right into a new order

explanation.surface: Most tired after correcting a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain's mischievous hero of the Mississippi river novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's fictional hero is a famously mischievous boy.

clue.text: Naming bird on heather

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Identifying a bird perched on the moorland heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a title to something is naming it.

clue.text: Added round about two pounds for fruit

indicators.note: about here means surrounding the following piece

parts.note: added, extra, is more
O is round in shape
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two extra pounds of weight on account of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark sour cherry is a fruit used in cooking.

clue.text: Given a little publicity, as is proper

indicators.note: a little of the word says only part of it is used

explanation.surface: Modest publicity is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful and allowed is proper in the sense of permitted.

clue.text: Finding business bad or atrocious in the city

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: atrocious, dreadfully done, says the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Finding commerce bad or terrible in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: CORDOBA is a city in southern Spain, famous for its mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordoba is a historic city in Andalusia, Spain.

clue.text: Some won't rest lest they lose support

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People who never stop for fear of losing their backing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the people who lose support are those who won't rest, but a trestle is literally a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame supporting a table top, a support in its own right.

clue.text: All in it turned colour

indicators.note: turned says the short word it is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour

explanation.surface: A whole thing turned a different shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted is all in, worn out.

clue.text: Release of underworld supremo by order

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
a charge is an order, an instruction

explanation.surface: A gang leader freed by a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld supremo' suggests a crime boss, but it is Dis, Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing a patient or prisoner is discharging them.

clue.text: One treats the German without rating

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the article surrounds the next piece

parts.note: der is a German word for the
OS, ordinary seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A German who gives medical care without any rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone administering medicine in measured amounts treats patients.

clue.text: Looks for small change in gardening equipment

indicators.note: in means the coin sits inside the tools

parts.note: hoes are garden tools
P, penny, is small change

explanation.surface: Searching for loose coins among the garden tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To look for something is to wish or expect it, so it is what one expects.

clue.text: Complaint made by one head about pupils

indicators.note: about here means going round the next piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a ness is a headland
L is a learner, so two of them are pupils

explanation.surface: A grievance from a head teacher regarding the students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a head teacher, but it is NESS, a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an ailment or disease.

clue.text: Knock the Left in sympathy

parts.note: a rap is a knock
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Criticising the political Left out of fellow feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Left' suggests politics, but it is the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A close harmonious bond of understanding is sympathy between people.

clue.text: Sound trader, though comparatively repellent

indicators.note: Sound means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a grocer is a food trader

explanation.surface: An honest shopkeeper who is nonetheless rather disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: More coarse or disgusting is the comparative of gross.

clue.text: The loss was before replacement of gate

indicators.note: before means it comes first in the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: replacement of means its letters are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: The loss happened before the gate was replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste or loss through use is the amount lost.
